_comment: Copy this file to assets.json and edit for your network. It gives ARP detection a trust anchor (so it names the impostor, not just 'a MAC changed'), enables rogue-device detection, and supplies the known-good baselines that Tier 2 exploit detection diffs against. main.py loads assets.json on startup; without it, ARP detection falls back to learn-on-first-sight and Tier 2 falls back to a learning window.
_hosts_comment: EVERY machine you want the strong reverse-shell rule to watch — not just servers. BEHAVIOR_UNEXPECTED_OUTBOUND is the only rule that catches a callback on an ALLOWED port (tcp/443), and it only watches hosts listed here. A host with no entry falls back to a port heuristic that exempts 80/443/22/8443 — precisely the ports an attacker picks to blend in. ('servers' is still accepted as an alias for this block.) Generate a starter list with: python baseline_assets.py --pcap capture.pcap

192.168.56.102.description: Metasploitable 2 — lab target (server: zero normal egress)
192.168.56.102._listening_ports_comment: Known-good port snapshot. A port answering SYN-ACK that is absent from this list fires BEHAVIOR_NEW_LISTENING_PORT (bind-shell indicator). Take it from a host you trust — `ss -ltnp` on the box — BEFORE any testing, not after.
192.168.56.102._allowed_outbound_comment: Destinations this host may legitimately reach, as [ip, port]. Keep it as short as you can defend — an empty list is the strongest baseline. Use null for the IP to allow a port to any destination (e.g. DNS).

192.168.56.20.description: Analyst workstation — legitimately talks to the Internet
192.168.56.20._comment: A workstation needs a WIDER allowlist than a server, but listing it is still far stronger than leaving it out: without an entry, a reverse shell to tcp/443 from this host is invisible to every port-based rule.

192.168.56.30.description: Host with no hand-written baseline yet
192.168.56.30._learn_outbound_comment: Opt in to learn-on-first-sight: watch this host's egress for outbound_learn_sec (default 300s), then treat anything new as anomalous. Findings are tagged baseline_source='learned'. Convenient, but it bakes in whatever was happening during the learning window — do NOT rely on it for a host that might already be compromised.

_scanners_comment: Hosts permitted to run reconnaissance (vulnerability scanners, monitoring). Their recon alerts are recorded at INFO severity with the original severity preserved on the alert — auditable, but not paging. An unlisted host running the same scan still alerts at full severity.
_shell_sessions_comment: Standing [client, server] exemptions for BEHAVIOR_INTERACTIVE_SHELL. A legitimate SSH session IS an interactive shell — identical on the wire — so the rule stays quiet only when something vouches for it. Preferred: deploy host_log_sensor.py on the server, and its SSH Login alerts vouch automatically. Use this list only for servers where the host sensor is NOT deployed; otherwise every real SSH session there raises a medium 'could not confirm this login' alert. Keep it narrow: a shell between an allowlisted pair is invisible to this rule.
